The term $\hat{\alpha}_k G_k^{2D}(\mathbf{p})$ represents the effective alpha of the $k$-th splat at the pixel [S12, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly provides the alpha compositing formula: $C(	extbf{p}) =  oldsymbol{sum}_{i in N}  oldsymbol{c}_i(	extbf{d}) lpha_i G_i^{2D}(	extbf{p})  igprod_{j<i}(1 - lpha_j G_j^{2D}(	extbf{p}))$. In this equation, the term $lpha_i G_i^{2D}(	extbf{p})$ represents the contribution of the $i$-th Gaussian (splat) to the pixel color, weighted by its opacity $lpha_i$ and its 2D Gaussian footprint $G_i^{2D}(	extbf{p})$. This product is the standard definition of the effective alpha (or transmittance contribution) of that specific splat at the pixel location in volume rendering. The claim uses the index $k$ instead of $i$, which is a standard notational variation, and refers to it as 'effective alpha', which accurately describes the term's role in the compositing equation.
